key_responsibilities: Design, develop, implement and fix features in codebase
Train and deploy new AI models
Analyze model performance and identify improvements
Research/evaluate emerging technologies to enhance AI models

strengths: TensorRT/CUDA inference optimization is real depth, not a keyword: COFFIN capstone hit 5.2x YOLO speedup (56.7 -> 10.9 ms) and the VGG16 project hand-wrote coalesced CUDA C++ conv kernels beating TorchScript CPU by ~35%.
Model deployment on constrained hardware is genuinely demonstrated: Jetson YOLO, ONNX/TFLite export at Tusk, 8-bit quantization on TinyLlama with <1% accuracy loss.

Robotics integration and validation is backed by physical hardware: UR5e collision-free pick-and-place via ROS 2 driver, AL5B <2mm repeatability, 100% pick reliability over 10 trials after resolving 11 integration failures.
Autonomous-driving domain exposure exists via the CARLA project (~5,000 YOLO + ~3,000 UFLD frames from semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering).
real_gaps: The binding requirement is 'Two years of industry experience in automotive industry software development.' Justin has 0 years full-time and no automotive employer. This is a stated minimum, not a preference.
No CI/CD pipeline experience anywhere in the profile. GitLab and Git are version control, not pipelines.
'Production-level software development' is unmet in the literal sense. Every entry is an internship, research fellowship, or academic project. Nothing shipped to a fleet or on-call service.
Perception here means AV perception at scale (multi-sensor, fleet data, large-scale training). Justin's perception work is single-camera object detection and monocular depth on desk-scale robots.

The posting has the structural hallmarks of a PERM labor-certification ad: a 'Ref. No. N322' printed twice, generic filler duties ('Connect/drive project-level impact through technology solutions..'), and a 'Requires... Experience must include:' enumerated qualification list. That format is written to match one specific incumbent already in the seat.
overstated_by_keywords: GPU training — SLURM cluster coursework and single-model fine-tuning, not multi-GPU distributed training at AV data scale.
Machine learning applications — broad but shallow across many one-off projects rather than sustained ownership of a model in production.
Testing/debugging algorithms — real debugging happened (the 11 COFFIN integration failures) but there is no formal test infrastructure or regression suite anywhere.
llm_analysis.reasoning: On skills alone this is one of the closest keyword matches in the pipeline: TensorRT, CUDA, PyTorch, C++, Python, model deployment and robotics integration are all genuinely backed by hardware projects rather than name-dropped. The blocker is not skill, it is shape. The req asks for two years of automotive-industry software development at a $165k-$198k band, and the posting reads like a green-card labor-certification ad rather than an open search. Skills say yes, the hiring gate says this is not a new-grad seat.
